about: Advisories this repository has looked at and decided not to act on yet.
Every entry is a dated decision, not a mute. `scripts/audit-gate.mjs` fails
the build when an entry passes its `expires` date, so tolerating an advisory
costs a review on a schedule rather than costing nothing forever. That is the
whole point of the file: a `--ignore` flag on a command line records no
reasoning, no author and no end date, and within a year nobody can tell
whether it is still true.
Fields, all required, all strings:
id         the advisory identifier -- RUSTSEC-YYYY-NNNN, or the GHSA id
ecosystem  "cargo" or "npm"
package    the package the advisory is against, so a re-used id cannot
silently widen the exemption to a different dependency
reason     why this was judged tolerable. Prose, and long enough to be a
justification rather than a restatement of the title -- the gate
rejects anything under 80 characters. Write it for the person
who has to decide whether to extend it.
reviewed   the date the reasoning below was established (YYYY-MM-DD)
expires    the date it must be re-established (YYYY-MM-DD)
reviewer   who made the call
To add one, fix the advisory first. Add an entry only when there is no fixed
release, or when upgrading is genuinely not possible yet. See
docs/supply-chain.md.

advisories.reason: The Marvin timing side-channel in rsa 0.9.x has no fixed release; RustSec has listed the advisory as unresolved since November 2023 and upstream has no patched version to move to. It is exempt here because the crate is not compiled into anything this repository ships: rsa reaches server/Cargo.lock through sqlx-mysql only, and sqlx is declared with features = ["runtime-tokio", "sqlite", "migrate"], so the MySQL driver is never built. `cargo tree --target all -e normal,build,dev -i rsa` prints nothing on any target, which is the check to repeat when this entry comes up for renewal. cargo audit reports it regardless because it reads the lockfile rather than the build graph, and a lockfile records every crate the resolver considered, compiled or not. If a future change ever enables sqlx's mysql feature, this exemption stops being true on the same day and must be removed rather than extended.

The timing variability is fixed only in crypto-bigint 0.7.6, which arrives with elliptic-curve 0.14 and p256 0.14. server reaches crypto-bigint 0.5.5 through elliptic-curve 0.13, which opaque-ke 4.0.1 (its latest stable release) still requires; the opaque-ke line built on elliptic-curve 0.14 is pre-release only (4.1.0-pre.2). Moving the password login stack onto a pre-release is a bigger risk than this advisory. Renew by checking whether opaque-ke has a stable release on elliptic-curve 0.14; once it does, upgrade opaque-ke and p256 together and delete this entry.

The fix is libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39.0 (bundled SQLite 3.54), but no released sqlx can resolve to it: sqlx-sqlite 0.8.6 and 0.9.0 both require libsqlite3-sys < 0.38, so even moving to sqlx 0.9 only reaches 0.37.0, which is still affected. The flaw needs a process to open a database file together with a sibling -wal file whose page size differs, both crafted by someone else; the attack vector is local and the impact is disclosure of uninitialized page-cache bytes. The server opens only the database file it created itself in its own data directory, plus its own backup snapshots (backup/mod.rs, read-only). Restoring a snapshot or migration archive from an untrusted party is the one path that could expose it, and operators should be told to restore only their own backups. Renew by checking whether a sqlx release now allows libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39; if so, upgrade sqlx and delete this entry. If none exists by then, consider a [patch] of sqlx-sqlite.
